text:
maria-support: FYI customer on Dedicated env (pool: ded-eu-3) hitting intermittent 429s during nightly ingest. They have reserved capacity (8 GPUs), steady QPS ~120 but periodic spikes to ~220 for ~1-2m -> 429s + tail latencies ~20-30s. Auth appears fine on their side. Anyone seen headroom mismatch like this?

devon-eng: Can you grab the exact response headers from a 429 and the pool config? Also: model + region + are they using streaming?

maria-support: Pasting client log snippet they shared:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-redwood-rate-limit: pool=ded-eu-3;limit=200;remaining=0;reset=167
x-redwood-suggested-fallback: redwood-xxl-q4
```
They're using streaming chunked responses with concurrency set to 12.

raj-runtime: Streaming + high concurrency is a common trigger. Our limiter counts aggregate token throughput; with many concurrent streams the token-bucket can drain faster than headroom replenishes, causing short nonlinear 429 bursts. Also check if KV-cache hits reduce actual throughput and skew kernel selection — that can change effective capacity. Quick checks: ask them to run the same load with streaming disabled or drop concurrency to 4 and see if 429s disappear. Also confirm `reserved_headroom_pct` on the pool.

support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-067.

devon-eng: Repro command they can run from staging (non-streaming vs streaming):
```
ab -n 240 -c 12 -T 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -p payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Watch `x-redwood-rate-limit` headers and client-side tail latency.

maria-support: Customer ran the non-streaming run and 429s disappeared. They also dropped concurrency -> 429s stopped. They want recommended fix (config vs code change) and whether this is an SLA-alignment issue.

raj-runtime: I'll pull the pool telemetry and config now. If `reserved_headroom_pct` is configured low (<15%) bursts can be rejected to preserve SLO; bumping to ~25% for high-burst customers is a common mitigation. Alternatives: enable autoscale-burst on that tenant, or add a route-level soft-fallback to the q4 variant shown in headers to avoid hard 429s. Note: autoscale bursts increase cost vs reserved headroom change which keeps billing predictable. I'll open an ENG-RUNTIME ticket linking these repros and logs.

tech-lead: Please include cost delta estimates in the ticket and a recommended rolling plan. Customer pre-approved a temporary headroom bump for tonight's window.

customer-ops: We'll schedule the controlled ramp at 02:00 UTC and run both streaming/high-concurrency and non-streaming tests. We'll report results and attach logs.

maria-support: Plan captured: 1) raj to validate pool config + open runtime ticket; 2) customer to run two controlled repros (streaming high-concurrency, non-streaming high-concurrency) and share headers/logs; 3) support to monitor for 2 hours after change. Assigning follow-ups. :thumbsup:
